constraints: Issue #1864 states external pull requests are not being accepted; maintainers implement in-house. This Scout output is a proposal only.

The crate must clear cargo deny without SKIP_PACKAGE_AGE_CHECK; AGENTS.md requires new Cargo.lock entries to be at least 7 days old. tree-sitter-php v0.25.2 has a GitHub release/tag date of 2026-11-19, about 8.4 days before this run; the crates.io publish time was not checked (no crates.io access). v0.25.1 (2026-10-06) is the safe fallback.

tree-sitter-php 0.25.2 depends only on tree-sitter-language 0.1 at runtime; tree-sitter 0.27 is a dev-dependency. The workspace pins tree-sitter 0.27.1, so no tree-sitter version conflict is expected (Cargo.lock already has tree-sitter-language 0.1.9).

Parsing goes through get_compiled_queries(), which looks up QUERY_CACHE built from supported_languages(). A language missing from that list fails with UnsupportedLanguage even when get_language_info() returns Some. css, yaml and markdown are missing from the list today.

DEFUSE_QUERY is an Option in LanguageInfo, so None compiles. It is required here by the issue scope and acceptance criteria (five query constants and a defuse test), and parser.rs compiles it whenever Some: a bad query fails the whole PHP language with QueryError. Its only consumer, extract_def_use_for_file, is test-only (doc: no production caller since the symbol tool removal).
Element consumer names are fixed: function, func_name/method_name, class, class_name/type_name. Other capture names fall back to field lookup.
No build or query compilation was run (read-only scout); all query drafts are unverified until cargo test runs.

approaches.name: A: Full issue scope, Java/Swift template (recommended)
approaches.description: Add php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY, DEFUSE_QUERY and kind-based extract_inheritance; register LANGUAGE_PHP in get_language_info and get_ts_language; add php to EXTENSION_MAP and supported_languages(); add the Cargo pins; inline unit tests in php.rs plus a queries_compile test; one integration test file; README update. Extension-function handlers left None.
pros: Same registry shape as Java and Swift, so reviewers see no new concepts
Query compile guard covers all five constants in one test
cons: extract_inheritance cannot copy java.rs's field-based walk; needs child-kind iteration
DEFUSE_QUERY has no production consumer, so its coverage is test-only
Largest diff of the three (about 8 files); needs a Cargo.lock regen and the 7-day age check

approaches.name: B: Minimal registry-first (defer DEFUSE and REFERENCE)
approaches.description: Ship ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY and extract_inheritance; set defuse_query and reference_query to None; skip the integration test. Follow-up issue for defuse.
pros: Still delivers functions, classes, interfaces, traits, enums, calls and imports
cons: Fails the five-constant requirement and the defuse acceptance criterion in #1864
Leaves the defuse path untested for PHP even though LanguageInfo supports it
Requires a second PR and a second Cargo.lock change later

approaches.name: C: Full scope with queries derived from upstream queries/tags.scm
approaches.description: Same files as A, but ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY and IMPORT_QUERY start from the grammar's own queries/tags.scm (fetched: class_declaration, interface_declaration, trait_declaration, function_definition, method_declaration, function_call_expression, scoped_call_expression, member_call_expression) and add a unit test that every definition kind in tags.scm is matched by ELEMENT_QUERY.
pros: Uses the grammar maintainers' own captures as an oracle, lowering the chance of a wrong node kind
Parity test catches future grammar drift on bump
cons: tags.scm uses @name/@definition.* captures, which parser_elements does not read; queries must be re-captured with the names the consumer expects
Adds a test that depends on the upstream file layout
Same file count and complexity as A, plus the parity test

recommendation: Approach A. It is the only option that meets every acceptance criterion in #1864 (five query constants, extract_inheritance, both registries, tests, README) while following the Java and Swift pattern. Two decisions carry the risk and should be settled before coding: (1) extract_inheritance walks base_clause and class_interface_clause by kind, because the grammar gives them no field names; (2) use LANGUAGE_PHP, not LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY, so the mixed HTML edge case parses. Take the parity check from C as an extra unit test if time allows. Pin tree-sitter-php 0.25.2 only if its crates.io publish date is at least 7 days old; otherwise pin 0.25.1. Also add php to supported_languages(), or parsing fails.

inheritance_walk_citation: Grammar source: tree-sitter-php 0.25.2, common/define-grammar.js (the php/grammar.js entry point includes it) and php/src/node-types.json, both fetched via gh api in Step 4. Walk: (1) class_declaration (define-grammar.js lines 365-374: `optional($.attribute_list), repeat($._modifier), keyword('class'), field('name', reserved('classes', $.name)), optional($.base_clause), optional($.class_interface_clause), field('body', $.declaration_list)`). Neither base_clause nor class_interface_clause is wrapped in a field, so child_by_field_name("superclass") (Java's pattern) returns None. In node-types.json the class_declaration children list includes 'base_clause' and 'class_interface_clause', and its fields are only attributes, body, name. (2) base_clause (lines 334-337: `seq(keyword('extends'), commaSep1($._name))`); its node-types entry has no fields and children name | qualified_name | relative_name. Each named child becomes one entry 'extends <source text>'. (3) class_interface_clause (lines 381-384: `seq(keyword('implements'), commaSep1($._name))`); no fields; same child kinds; each named child becomes 'implements <source text>'. (4) _name is hidden, so children surface as name, qualified_name or relative_name. Result for `class Foo extends Bar implements A, B {}`: ["extends Bar", "implements A", "implements B"]; for `class Plain {}`: []. Upstream queries/tags.scm (fetched) uses the same shape: `(class_interface_clause [(name) (qualified_name)] @name) @reference.implementation`. Interface: base_clause children map to 'extends'. Enum (lines 339-347): only class_interface_clause, no base_clause. Trait: neither.
